name: Gradient boosting on engineered features (G-Research crypto competition)

origin.authors: G-Research and Kaggle competitors (Meme Lord Capital, Nathaniel Maddux, GABA)

how_it_works.simple: You turn price history into many hints, like how far price is from its recent average, and let a tree-based model learn which hints predict the next 15 minutes.
how_it_works.analogy: Like a weather forecaster who combines dozens of small clues (wind, clouds, pressure) instead of relying on one.
how_it_works.precise: Predict 15-minute residualized returns for 14 coins from minute bars with LightGBM on lagged price, volume and moving-average features; validate with walk-forward grouped folds with gaps. Scored by weighted Pearson correlation over three months of live data.

rule: Every minute, compute lagged return and moving-average-ratio features per coin, predict the 15-minute residual return with a LightGBM model retrained on an expanding window, and hold positions proportional to the cross-sectionally demeaned prediction.
data_needed: Minute OHLCV for liquid coins (Kaggle dataset or exchange APIs)
Coin weights for the residualized target
economic_rationale: Short-horizon return predictability in crypto from reversal, momentum and cross-asset lead-lag can be captured by nonlinear models; G-Research notes feature work mattered more than model choice.
why_it_might_fail: Winning live correlations in such competitions are small and the leaderboard was noisy, so ranks partly reflect luck. 15-minute signals need very low costs, and the edge may vanish after fees.

reported_results.source: G-Research, Wrapping up the G-Research Crypto Forecasting competition
reported_results.notes: All top three used LightGBM; feature engineering mattered more than models; leaderboard fluctuated a lot. Winning correlation scores were not stated on the pages read, so no number is given.

post_publication_evidence: Live scoring was part of the competition itself (three months after submissions closed). No later trading results from the winning models were found.

implementations.notes: LightGBM pipelines with walk-forward evaluation; not competition code.

relevance.reason: LightGBM on engineered features with walk-forward validation is the most practical ML baseline parity could run on FX and commodities.
